articles.headline: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, sources say
articles.description: The Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The move came a day after the Cardinals gave up 34 points to the Kansas City Chiefs, the second-straight game Arizona allowed 34 points and the eighth time in 11 games this season that the defense gave up 30 or more.

Senior defensive assistant coach Teryl Austin is expected to take over as interim defensive coordinator, sources added.

After Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City, coach Mike LaFleur said he knows the Cardinals' defense could be better.

"I thought they had a good plan with some things to beat the pressure so that when that's the case, we got to be able to rush with four and cover," LaFleur said. "And I know we're capable of doing that better. I know we're capable of stopping the run better than we did particularly early. I mean they only finished with 118 [rushing yards], but it kind of started early where they were getting some of those gashes, and I thought we honed in there toward the end, but it was too late."

Rallis, 33, was hired by former Cardinals coach Jonathan Gannon to be Arizona's defensive coordinator in 2023 and was retained by LaFleur in February.

Multiple sources told ESPN that Arizona had attempted to move on from Rallis during the offseason. However, Arizona's options at defensive coordinator were limited with LaFleur being the last head coach hired during the 2026 coaching cycle. The team did discuss those limited options to replace Rallis, one source said.

"A lot of jobs are filled up, and a lot of things have been filled," the source said. "So, you try to look at what all the options are, and in the end, Nick was the one that made the most sense."

This season, Rallis guided a defense that was ranked 32nd in points margin per game, 31st in opponent points per game, 29th in opponent yards, and 28th in yard margin per game and opponent turnovers.

The Cardinals' defense was also ranked last in the NFL in opponent-adjusted QBR and 31st in raw QBR. It was 27th in run yards allowed per game, and 26th in yards per game and yards per play.

Rallis' defenses have struggled to stop offenses from scoring going back to last season.

Since Week 10 of 2025, which was the first in a nine-game losing streak to end the season, the Cardinals' defense ranked 32nd in opponent points, opponent points per game, point margin, point margin per game and opponent yards; 29th in opponent yards per game; and 28th in yard margin and yard margin per game.

Arizona's defense has given up 30 or more points in 14 of its past 20 games.

The Cardinals, winless (0-4) at home under LaFleur, play host to the Washington Commanders on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.headline: Giants' Greg Newsome out 'multiple weeks' with ankle sprain
articles.description: Giants starting cornerback Greg Newsome will miss "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, coach John Harbaugh said Monday.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants starting cornerback Greg Newsome will miss "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, coach John Harbaugh said Monday.

A decision has not been made about whether Newsome will need surgery. If he lands on injured reserve, he must miss at least four games.

Newsome was hurt while being blocked on a running play on the opening drive of Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. He left MetLife Stadium in a boot and underwent further testing Monday morning.

"He's got a high ankle sprain. It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh said. "It's going to be multiple weeks."

Newsome is in his first year with the Giants. He's started nine games and has 35 tackles, eight passes defensed and one interception while being an integral player in coordinator Dennard Wilson's defense.

The veteran cornerback signed a three-year, $36 million contract extension last month and was playing some of the best football of his career. He credited the system and the Giants maximizing his strengths in man coverage.

In his absence, veteran Paulson Adebo stepped into the lineup for the remainder of the contest Sunday. He had four passes defensed and earned Harbaugh's praise for his performance.

"I thought he played great football. He got a game ball. He was one of the game-ball guys," Harbaugh said. "I think he's a legitimate corner in this league. All he's done is just put his head down and get to work every single day and work his tail off, work through his issue injury wise, got in great shape through all of that, practices every day, doesn't complain -- even last week when he was inactive, which was a tough call a little bit, special teams-wise, yet, didn't say a word, just said, 'Hey, I've got you coach. I'm ready.' Comes out today, plays the whole game like the top-level corner that he is, he's proven to be. I agree with you, I thought he played at the highest level."

articles.headline: Sources: Giants DC Dennard Wilson interviews for HC job at alma mater Maryland
articles.description: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview recently for the vacant head coaching job at Maryland, sources told NFL Network.
articles.body:
New York Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview recently for the vacant head coaching job at Maryland, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

A Maryland native and former defensive back for the Terrapins, Wilson is the latest potential candidate to coach at his alma mater. Maryland has been seeking a new coach since firing Mike Locksley last month.

Brian Kelly, the former head coach at LSU, Notre Dame and Cincinnati, said earlier this month that he interviewed for the Maryland job. The Terrapins are 4-7 overall this season and 2-6 in Big Ten play.

Wilson is in his first season with the Giants after spending the past two seasons as the defensive coordinator for the Tennessee Titans.

"No level of concern that it will interrupt our season at all," Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday. "None."

The Giants aren't at the point of thinking about any contingency plans as they don't expect Wilson to leave during the season, even if he were to eventually be offered the job.

"Yeah, he's not going to leave the Giants to go in the middle of the season to take the Maryland job," Harbaugh said. "I don't know if he'll take the job or not. He's a Maryland grad. Kind of getting ahead of ourselves. We'll cross that bridge when we get there."

The first-place Giants (6-3-1) are tied with the Chicago Bears for seventh in the NFL in total defense and are coming off an outstanding defensive performance in their victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, when they intercepted Trevor Lawrence twice and sacked the star quarterback three times.

Wilson, 44, was an all-conference honorable mention selection during his senior season with the Terrapins and returned to the school for two years as a graduate assistant in 2007-08 before entering the NFL coaching ranks in 2012.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Kevin De Bruyne: Man City achievements will not be tainted if appeal fails
articles.description: Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.
articles.body:
Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.

De Bruyne won a host of honours, including six Premier League crowns and the Champions League, during a glorious 10-year spell at City that ended when he joined Napoli in 2025.

A shadow has since been cast over City's most successful era after the club were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations in September.

Among the punishments City could face if they fail in an appeal is the removing of some of their honours.

De Bruyne, 35, said he remains proud of the part he played in those triumphs and retains huge affection for the club's owners.

De Bruyne, who is back at the Etihad Stadium as Napoli face City in the Champions League on Tuesday, said at a news conference: "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club, I love the owners.

"I've even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club.

"I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change, [the way] the people treated me and my family for 10 years.

"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit. I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most.

"I've given my all and that's not going to change in my mind. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

"But everybody has their own opinion, I guess. Other people may be 'disgraced' a bit, but I can't change anything about that."

De Bruyne's return to Manchester comes amid reports he is unsettled at Napoli and could seek a move in January.

He did not address his future or speculation about tensions with coach Massimiliano Allegri and some teammates, but he did express frustration at the media reaction to comments by his wife about life in Naples.

He said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed. A lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house -- I don't think it is OK.

"But it is what it is. Some press created this in Italy, I don't know why. Nobody knows my life, you will never know. It has not been nice for my wife, for my family."

Asked about De Bruyne's future, Allegri said: "As far as Kevin is concerned, we have not spoken about that because at the moment we are caught up in all of these games.

"Over Christmas there will be a short break then the transfer window will open and the club will be open to try and bring in reinforcements. Then it is down to the players and who wants to leave."

articles.headline: Fantasy adds, NBA bets to make for Monday: Pick up Brook Lopez, Quentin Grimes
articles.description: Andre Snellings breaks down Monday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
This NBA week opens with 10 games on the docket and one anticipated season debut from an All Star. Brandon Ingram is expected to make his first appearance of the season for the LA Clippers in their road tilt against the Houston Rockets. Ingram has been out recovering from offseason surgery on a partially torn Achilles tendon, but has ramped up his activity and should be on the court tonight. It hasn't been announced what type of minutes restriction he might be on, but after such a lengthy layoff some sort of minutes regimen should be expected.

The Clippers and the Rockets comprise one of the six games tonight featuring spreads of at least 8.5 points, with five of those spreads in double figures. The larger spreads indicate that several games have anticipated blowout potential, and blowouts can be challenging for both fantasy production and player props.

As such, it could be worth looking more closely at the three games featuring spreads of only 3.5 points tonight. The Memphis Grizzlies at the Charlotte Hornets, the Portland Trail Blazers at the Philadelphia 76ers and the Phoenix Suns at the New Orleans Pelicans are all expected to be closer, competitive games tonight. The Trail Blazers at the 76ers is the only game tonight between two teams that are both over .500, while the Suns at the Pelicans is the only game with a spread under four and an over/under line set above 230 (232.5 total).

These, and many other storylines will be on display in tonight's action. As always, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some potential fantasy streamers and betting angles of interest.

Fantasy stream team

Available in at least 50% of ESPN leagues.

Jalen Smith, PF/C, Chicago Bulls (rostered in 49.1% of ESPN leagues)

Smith returned from his one-game absence (illness) with a bang on Sunday, dropping 26 points with two blocks and two steals in 34 minutes. Over his past six games, Smith has averaged 18.7 PPG, 7.5 RPG and 3.2 3PG.

Quentin Grimes, SG/SF, Los Angeles Lakers (44.7%)

Grimes is expected to get his fifth straight start tonight in place of Austin Reaves (heel). Grimes popped for a career-high 47 points last Wednesday, and overall in his past four games he has averaged 25.5 PPG, 6.0 RPG and 5.0 3PG. He has slotted in perfectly as the second offensive option for the Lakers next to Luka Doncic.

Cam Spencer, SG/PG, Memphis Grizzlies (37.5%)

Spencer moved back to a reserve role when Ty Jerome returned from a four-game absence, but he still played 30 minutes and notched more than 30 fantasy points for the fifth straight game. In fact, in his past three appearances off the bench, Spencer has averaged 12.9 PPG, 4.3 APG and 2.0 3PG in 24.7 MPG.

Brook Lopez, C, LA Clippers (38.6%)

Lopez enters this game on a torrid scoring stretch, having notched 20 or more points in six of his last eight games including the last three straight. He has been particularly hot from behind the arc, averaging 2.3 3PG on 41.9 3P% to go along with 18.5 PPG and 5.8 RPG

articles.headline: Fantasy risers and fallers: Trade Davion Mitchell? Move on from De'Aaron Fox?
articles.description: Steve Alexander looks at three players on the rise and three who are slumping and how fantasy managers should react.
articles.body:
Davion Mitchell is turning heads and leading the league in assists, Quentin Grimes is on a heater in Los Angeles and Cedric Coward is quickly emerging as a fantasy force. All are moving up the fantasy rankings.

Meanwhile, Kel'el Ware's stint for the 1-16 Bucks has been a nightmare, Jalen Green is not pulling his weight in Phoenix and De'Aaron Fox has really struggled in San Antonio. Which ones should you move on from at this point?

Risers and Fallers helps you track hot players who are worth holding onto, players are are likely overvalued right now (see the final paragraph under Risers), as well as struggling players you might be better off without. Here's more on each of these players.

Resources: Rankings | Adds/Drops | Scoring leaders | Player Rater | Mock draft lobby | Depth charts | Schedule | Injuries

Risers

 Davion Mitchell, Heat PG, (86.8% rostered in ESPN leagues)

Mitchell was drafted around the 10th round in most of my 12-team drafts and he's shocking the world, leading the league in assists and appearing to love playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. His November numbers include 17.5 points, 8.9 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.7 blocks and 2.7 triples, while hitting 52.6% of his shots.

This might seem to scream "trade him before the bottom falls out," but I don't think that's the case. You likely drafted him very late in your draft (or even got him off the waiver wire) and he's also been one of your best players all season. Especially over the last two weeks, when he's been a Top 10 fantasy player. I'm holding onto Mitchell until further notice and I think he's very driven to win the assist title this season. And with guys like Bam Adebayo and Giannis to throw it to, he should continue to do this all year. Ride the wave.

 Quentin Grimes, Lakers SG/SF, (45.7% rostered)

I sadly wrote that Sandro Mamukelashvili was a Riser last week, but things have changed a lot since then. Grimes has been on fire with Austin Reaves (heel) and Luka Doncic (rest) missing games, but that's not the main reason he's cooking right now.

He scored 22 points last Sunday and then exploded for a career-high 47 against Charlotte on Tuesday. He then scored 20 and 13 points in each of his last two games and is averaging a ridiculous 25.5 points, 5.0 3-pointers, 6.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists over his last four.

Sure, he'll take a hit once Reaves is back, but the Lakers are going to be careful with Reaves and we've already seen them give Luka and Walker Kessler the occasional night off. But the most important point here is that I suspect Luka has figured out the Lakers are a better team when Grimes is cooking, and he's become his new go-to guy after Reaves and Kessler, shoving Mamukelashvili out of the way. And that means that Grimes should be a solid fantasy player all season. If you've got him, hang onto him rather than trying to capitalize on his recent success. Hopefully, he's just getting started.

articles.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson needs season-ending ankle surgery, Sean McVay says
articles.description: Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson's ankle injury will require season-ending surgery.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson's ankle injury will require season-ending surgery, head coach Sean McVay said Monday.

Ferguson has been on injured reserve since spraining his ankle in Week 3. The Rams opened his 21-day practice window on Nov. 4 with the intent of him playing against the Washington Commanders that Sunday.

But Ferguson injured his hamstring in practice that Friday, putting him out a couple more weeks. On Nov. 11, McVay said the team's goal was to have a roster spot open for the tight end by the time the practice window closed, even if he wasn't ready to play.

But on Monday, McVay said Ferguson's ankle is "just not responding the way that you want." The tight end will not be added to the active roster before the end of his 21-day practice window, which will end his season.

McVay was asked whether Ferguson had a setback with his ankle injury.

"I think it was more along the lines of pushing to get back, didn't necessarily feel great, but he had a really good week of practice," McVay said. "But you could still see it was kind of getting comfortable, took some meds to be able to do that, gets the hamstring on the Friday.

"And then as he's really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it and it was like something in his deltoid in his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want, unfortunately. And so as a result of that, I don't know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it's just not coming along and he wouldn't be able to be himself."

Ferguson was a second-round pick in the 2025 draft. In 17 career games, he has 18 catches for 294 yards and four touchdowns.

The Rams play the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game, which kicks off the Week 12 slate.

articles.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
articles.description: The UEFA Champions League is going at full speed, and we're beyond the halfway point of the league phase. Injuries are starting to pile up. Where does your club rank?
articles.body:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.

So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN (no change)

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2

- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)

Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.

PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.

They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).

2. BARCELONA (no change)

- Previous rank: 2

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2

- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)

articles.headline: Oli McBurnie is Hull's 'Braveheart,' says Sergej Jakirovic after Brighton win
articles.description: Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic has likened striker Oli McBurnie to Scottish warrior William Wallace, as depicted by Mel Gibson in the 1995 film Braveheart.
articles.body:
Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic has likened striker Oli McBurnie to Scottish warrior William Wallace, as depicted by Mel Gibson in the 1995 film Braveheart.

McBurnie scored two goals in stoppage time as Hull shocked high-flying Brighton 2-0 at home on Sunday.

McBurnie's resurgence has also seen him recalled to the Scotland squad, and Jakirovic was not shy in his praise for the 30-year-old.

He named him as a crucial member of his team, with Regan Slater, Lewie Coyle, Matt Crooks and John Egan also credited for the roles they are playing at the club.

"It is normal to him, he's in the Scottish national team. He is Braveheart, like the movie," Jakirovic said of McBurnie's late goals and never-say-die attitude.

"He's excellent, there is no doubt about Oli, ever. I never have any doubt about Oli McBurnie because he is a natural leader.

"He doesn't need telling, he is leading the team together with Slater, Coyle and Crooksy -- John Egan is there too.

"They are very, very important to us."

articles.description: — Brandin Podziemski had 18 points and seven rebounds and the Golden State Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by holding off Boston for an 88-87 win Sunday night, sending the Celtics to their first four-game skid in five years.
